Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Saurabh Shyam Shamshery,J.
1. Heard Sri Gyanendra Prasad Mahant, learned counsel for applicant and Sri Roshan Kumar Singh,
learned AGA for State.

2. Applicant-Suraj Basor has approached this Court by way of filing present bail application seeking enlargement on bail in Case Crime No. 1096 of 2022, under Sections 498A, 304B IPC and 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station Nandgram, District Ghaziabad.

3. This application was filed on 04.03.2023 and was taken up for hearing earlier on seven days,
however, it was adjourned mainly to complete pleadings or on request of learned counsel for applicant.

sentences.text: Applicant before this Court is husband of deceased, who is facing trial for offence of demand of dowry and dowry death.
It was a love marriage.
Wife of applicant was got admitted in hospital by applicant since she suffered head injury due to fall from a staircase.

She was admitted on 03.12.2022 in Jagannath Multispeciality Hospital, Ghaziabad and from their she was brought to UCMS and GTB Hospital, Delhi on 04.12.2022 and during course of management she died on 07.12.2022.
5. As per post mortem report cause of death was cranio cerebral damage as a result of ante mortem injury to head produced by blunt force/ surface impact.
Viscera was preserved, however, according to instructions of parties, result thereof is not on record.

Details of ante mortem injuries are as follows:
"Stitched wound of size 2.0cm x 0.5cm obliquely present over right side of head, 3.0 cm away from mid line and 14.0cm above right eyebrow with six stitches present in situ.
On removal of stitches margins of wound are irregular, separable, abraded and contused, wound is bone deep."
6. Learned counsel for applicant submits that applicant is in jail since 11.12.2022, i.e., for about one year and five months.
It was an accidental fall and applicant immediately took her wife to hospital and provided best treatment according to his financial capacity.

He further submits that immediately applicant informed about the occurrence to family members of deceased, who were present during treatment, inquest report as well as during post mortem, however, no suspicion was raised.
7. Learned counsel further submits that last rite of deceased took place on 09.12.2022 (died on 07.12.2022) and FIR was lodged on the next day, i.e., 10.12.2022 (after three days of death).
Learned counsel further submits that delay in lodging FIR remained unexplained.
8. Learned counsel for applicant also refers a manuscript of conversation between deceased and her mother after the occurrence that she fall from staircase though no dying declaration was recorded.
Applicant has also moved an application to make the aforesaid manuscript to be part of case diary but according to his instructions it was not made part of case diary.
Learned counsel submits that allegations of demand of dowry are not sustainable since it was a love marriage, therefore, there was no possibility of demand of dowry.
9. Learned AGA appearing for State has opposed the prayer for bail and submits that all ingredients of dowry death are prima facie exist.

He further submits that genesis of occurrence was suppressed and it was not immediately informed to police, therefore, despite victim was in a position to speak,
her statement was not recorded.

10. I have considered the above mentioned rival submissions in referred factual and legal backgrounds and in view of established principle of jurisprudence of bail i.e 'bail is rule and jail is exception' as well as relevant factors for consideration of a bail application such as (i) whether there is any prima facie or reasonable ground to believe that the accused had committed the offence; (ii)
nature and gravity of the accusation (iii) severity of the punishment in the event of conviction; (iv)
Suraj Basor vs State Of U.P. on 10 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94159206/
2 danger of the accused absconding or fleeing, if released on bail; (v) character, behaviour, means,
position and standing of the accused; (vi) likelihood of the offence being repeated; (vii) reasonable apprehension of the witnesses being influenced; (viii) danger, of course of justice being thwarted by grant of bail etc, and that an order to grant or not to grant bail must assigned reasons (see Deepak Yadav vs State of U.P. (2022) 8 SCC 559, Manoj Kumar Khokar vs State of Rajasthan and Anr (2022) 3 SCC 501, The State of Jharkhand vs Dhananjay Gupta @ Dhananjay Prasad Gupta: Order dated 7.11.2023 in SLP(Crl) No.10810/2023, Shiv Kumar Vs The State of U.P. and Ors : Order dated 12.9.2023 in Criminal Appeal No.2782 of 2023; Ramayan Singh vs. The State of U.P. and another,
2024 SCC OnLine SC 563), I am of considered opinion that present is a fit case to grant bail to applicant mainly on following grounds:-
(a) Applicant before this Court is husband of deceased and in jail since 11.12.2022.
Court takes note that it is his consistent case that deceased died due to accidental fall.

sentences.text: (b) Injured remained in hospital for about three days, however, Court takes note of argument that complainant/ informant has not raised any suspicion about occurrence.
(c) Court also takes note the submission that applicant has provided immediate medical treatment to his wife and even she was referred to a better hospital at Delhi where she died.
(d) In aforesaid circumstances, Court takes note that there is delay of three days in lodging of FIR and explanation thereof may not be sufficient.

11. The applicant is directed to remain present on each and every date as and when required by Trial Court during trial and in case any application for exemption on vague ground is filed, the same shall be a ground for Trial Court to cancel bail immediately.

12. Let the applicant-Suraj Basor be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Court concerned with the following conditions which are being imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not harm or harass the victim/complainant in any manner whatsoever.
(ii) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment or exemption from appearance on the date fixed in trial.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(iii) The applicant will not misuse the liberty of bail in any manner whatsoever.
In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C., may be issued and

if applicant fails Suraj Basor vs State Of U.P. on 10 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94159206/
3 to appear before the Court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then, the Trial Court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law, under section 174-A I.P.C.
(iv) The Trial Court may make all possible efforts/endeavour and try to conclude the trial expeditiously, preferably within a period of six months after release of applicant,
if there is no other legal impediment.

sentences.text: 13. The identity, status and residential proof of sureties will be verified by Court concerned and in case of breach of any of the conditions mentioned above, Court concerned will be at liberty to cancel the bail and send the applicant to prison.

14. The bail application is allowed.
15.
It is made clear that the observations made hereinabove are only for the purpose of adjudicating the present bail application.
